title: Failover-test: Docker Swarm manager (host-level outage)
description: Drives a Docker Swarm manager-loss scenario by SUSPENDING the current Swarm-leader VM at the host level (vmrun suspend) — not a graceful service stop, a real outage. Measures the heartbeat-detection-bound RTO, then resumes the VM.

observe.what: scenario tag · original leader · new leader · RTO seconds (longer than Consul/Nomad — heartbeat-detection-bound) · recovery state
Cluster view briefly shows the suspended manager as `Down`, then `Ready` after vmrun resume

whatProves: Docker Swarm's manager raft tolerates a hard host-level outage of the leader VM; the CLI captures the heartbeat-detection RTO (observed ~21.59s in 0.3.2) — meaningfully slower than service-level kills, which is the realistic DR characteristic to know.
